harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured HTTPS on node1:8443 via nginx with a self-signed, short-lived (6-minute) certificate, a systemd oneshot service (cert-renew.service) + timer (cert-renew.timer, 60s interval) that regenerates the cert before it expires (checkend 180s threshold) and runs `systemctl reload nginx` (zero-downtime reload, does not drop existing connections) so nginx picks up each new cert. Opened firewalld port 8443/tcp. Verified two independent automatic renewals occurred (before and after a full node reboot), each producing a new certificate serial that was immediately served over live TLS handshakes, with HTTPS continuously returning 200 throughout. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol: captured baseline boot_id, rebooted node1 via `systemctl reboot`, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified nginx, the renewal timer, and HTTPS/cert rotation all recovered and continued functioning correctly post-reboot.
actions_performed: Installed nginx via dnf on node1 (CentOS Stream 10)
Wrote /usr/local/bin/renew-cert.sh: generates a short-lived (6 min) self-signed cert via openssl when <180s validity remains, atomically swaps files, and reloads nginx only if active
Created /etc/nginx/tls/node.env holding NODE_IP for the renewal script's SAN
Generated the initial certificate and configured /etc/nginx/conf.d/https-8443.conf to listen on 8443 with ssl_certificate/ssl_certificate_key pointing at the rotating cert/key files
Enabled and started nginx; opened firewalld port 8443/tcp permanently
Created systemd unit cert-renew.service (oneshot) and cert-renew.timer (OnBootSec=30s, OnUnitActiveSec=60s, Persistent=true), enabled and started the timer
Observed and verified an automatic renewal (serial and notAfter changed) with nginx reload and continuous HTTP 200 responses
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, service state, live TLS serial, HTTP 200)
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect), polled until exec was available again
Verified boot_id changed confirming an actual restart
Verified nginx and cert-renew.timer came back active post-reboot, HTTPS serving 200 with the persisted certificate
Observed a second automatic renewal after reboot, with the new serial served live over TLS and HTTP still returning 200 throughout

evidence.summary: nginx config validated, listening on 0.0.0.0:8443/[::]:8443, firewalld port opened, curl returns http_code=200 over TLS

Baseline cert serial/expiry captured at 10:01:27; cert-renew.timer fired and renew-cert.sh automatically issued a new cert (new serial, extended notAfter) at 10:04:39, logged in /var/log/renew-cert.log and confirmed via systemctl status of the oneshot service

evidence.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests
evidence.summary: Immediately after the automatic renewal, curl to :8443 still returned 200, and a live TLS handshake (openssl s_client) served the exact new certificate serial, proving nginx reloaded and picked up the rotated cert without downtime
Captured boot_id 83a0a80f-773c-4f3e-9137-1e7aa887b07a, nginx/cert-renew.timer active, HTTPS 200, live cert serial matching renewed cert
Issued backgrounded `systemctl reboot` on node1 so the exec call returned before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity proving restart occurred
evidence.summary: After polling through connection timeouts/resets while the node was down, exec succeeded again and boot_id changed to ee5486d2-7701-4036-a9ac-7525a4e03daf (new uptime since 10:05:10), proving an actual reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required services, data, and functionality
evidence.summary: Post-reboot: nginx and cert-renew.timer both active (enabled units auto-started), HTTPS serving 200 with the persisted cert/key, and a fresh automatic renewal (new serial 25112A49...) occurred and was served live via TLS with continuous 200 responses, confirming full end-to-end recovery of the certificate-rotation automation
